data.name: Divakar
data.gender_notes: Divakar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Divakar is a Sanskrit name derived from 'diva' meaning 'light' and 'kar' meaning 'doer'. In Hindu mythology, Divakar is the name of the sun god, Surya, who is responsible for illuminating the world with his light. The name Divakar carries the meaning “God of light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Divakar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Divakar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Divakar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Divakar represents the illuminating power of knowledge and wisdom, as well as the cultural symbol of light and enlightenment. In Hindu culture, the sun is revered as a symbol of power and authority, and the name Divakar carries these traditional meanings and values.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Divakar holds profound significance as an embodiment of truth, knowledge, and self-illumination. The sun god, Surya, is believed to be the source of all energy and the giver of life. Divakar signifies one's inner light that illuminates the path to spiritual growth and an enlightened consciousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Divakar: God of knowledge and wisdom. Light bearer, illuminating the path towards truth and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Divakar was a prominent Jain scholar and monk in the 12th century CE in India. He wrote several commentaries on Jain texts and is known for his contributions to Jain philosophy and literature.
Divakar is also mentioned in the 16th century CE Hindu epic 'Ramayana' as the name of the sage who blessed Lord Rama before his departure to the forest.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
